title: Fractional versus Integral Trek Linkage in Latent-Subgraph Causal Identification
banked_reason: Delivered tier subfield < floor field; not salvageable within scope.
gap_reasons: It does not characterize the advertised max-flow frontier: reachable predecessor closure is only sufficient, and calls outside that class—including much of the observed-to-latent setting—still require the original integer test.
The obstruction is only edge-deletion-minimal for fixed sources and terminals, not globally minimal or representative of a forbidden-configuration theory.

The package also provides no systematic benchmark evidence showing how frequently the proved closure tests apply or how much computation they save on substantive causal models, which limits its leading-journal significance.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery verified a legal LSC-induced half-integral counterexample, its fixed-terminal/source edge-deletion minimality, and an exact ordinary-max-flow reduction under reachable predecessor closure; both math and decision panels passed without findings. The field-tier framing collapsed because the closure theorem is sufficient rather than necessary-and-sufficient, and closing that gap, proving global minimality, or adding representative benchmarks would require new research.
tldr: Full fractional value does not in general certify the trek linkage required by latent-subgraph causal identification: an acyclic, legally reached exact doubled LSC call has \(\nu_{\mathrm{LP}}=K=2\) but \(\nu_{\mathrm{IP}}=1\), refuting the universal Conjecture~4.3 by an instance inside the published model.  Nevertheless, reachable predecessor closure after terminal pruning reduces the exact integer decision to one ordinary node-capacitated maximum flow.  In particular, every graph with no observed-to-latent arrows admits this reduction for every LSC call, and for fixed \(k\) the bounded-separator search makes \(\mathcal O(n^{k+2}m^k)\) candidate calls when \(n=|O|\) and \(m=|L|\) are positive.  This tractable regime permits arbitrary latent subgraphs but is a proper structural subclass of Sturma and Drton's arbitrary directed observed--latent model, not a characterization of their full class or of the maximal integral frontier.
gap: Sturma and Drton's Algorithm 1 uses an integer program, while Conjecture 4.3 proposes that full LP value always suffices. Their conjecture is stated for arbitrary graph/subgraph pairs, but the causally decisive question is whether it survives the exact doubled networks, candidate restrictions, and solved-node histories produced by LSC. No located public source resolves that question or gives a broader max-flow class beyond latent-factor graphs.
fill: Establish a reproducible realized obstruction, prove fixed-specification deletion minimality, derive a one-max-flow equivalence under predecessor closure, translate it to the ancestral no-re-entry class, and give a sound hybrid certificate protocol.
